sentences.text: Now the maneuvering signals, and we’ll take the International rules first, because they’re the simpler idea.
Under the International rules, when vessels are in sight of one another, a power-driven vessel that maneuvers tells everyone what she’s doing, as she does it.
One short blast: I am altering my course to starboard.
Two short blasts: I am altering my course to port.
Three short blasts: I am operating astern propulsion.
Here’s how I keep them straight.
One syllable, star-board comes first, so one blast.
Port is the other, so two.
And three means my engines are going astern.
Notice the wording: I am altering.
It’s a statement of action, not a question, so no reply is required.
A vessel may back these up with a light: an all-round white light, flashing the same pattern.
Each flash is about one second, with about a second between flashes, and at least ten seconds between signals.
